significance.root_decision: For every p > 1 there is r0 with p - 1 < r0 < p such that, for 0 < r <= p, the Fuss-Catalan distribution mu(p, r) is unimodal if and only if r = p or r <= r0. Lean proves this for the measure with the explicit density of the source's Proposition 1.1, formula (2) (due to Forrester and Liu), with unimodality in the source's sense (an atom plus a density nondecreasing before and nonincreasing after the mode). That this measure is the moment-defined distribution mu(p, r), total mass one included, is the source's published Proposition 1.1, cited and not checked in Lean. The proof shows that the logarithmic derivative of the density is strictly decreasing in r, so the unimodal parameters form an interval, and locates its endpoint strictly between p - 1 and p.
significance.caveat: The Lean statement is tied to the source's object by a cited published theorem, not by Lean: Lean classifies the measure with the explicit density; its identification with the moment-defined mu(p, r), normalization included, is the source's Proposition 1.1 (Forrester and Liu 2015, Proposition 2.1). Two reviewers confirmed numerically that this density has mass one and the first Raney moments. Bounded literature search only. Cross-model confidence: correct 0.97, not public 0.85, not routine 0.65, Lean statement equals the printed conjecture modulo the cited proposition 0.95. The proof is short once the monotonicity in r is seen. The author packet's own report calls it PARTIAL relative to an earlier endpoint that included normalization.
